purpose: Brigatinib is used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is specifically used when your cancer has a change (mutation) in a gene called ALK. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein made by the faulty ALK gene that tells them to grow out of control. Brigatinib works like a key that blocks this protein, essentially turning off the signal that makes cancer cells grow and multiply. This helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting are common, especially early on. You may also notice fatigue, headache, cough, or rash. Some people experience high blood pressure, muscle pain, or changes in their vision. Blood sugar and certain enzyme levels in your blood may also go up.
warnings: A serious lung problem called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis can happen, sometimes within the first week. Tell your doctor right away if you have new or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever. This medicine can also cause high blood pressure, slow heart rate, liver problems, high blood sugar, and harm to an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment. Do not take it with certain other medications without checking with your doctor first.
typical_dosing: You usually start at a lower dose of 90 mg taken by mouth once a day for the first 7 days. If you tolerate it well, your doctor will increase your dose to 180 mg once a day. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food, and swallow the tablet whole.
